lines: This is Agent HQ.
An AI software team that lives on your desktop.
You describe what you want. The team plans it, builds it, and reviews it.
And you see every change before it lands.
Every task follows the same path.
You ask. Sovereign plans. You approve.
The agents build it, Sentinel reviews it, and you read the changes.
Meet the team.
Sovereign is the orchestrator. It's not a separate product, just the name of Agent HQ's lead agent.
It talks to you and plans the work.
Aegis designs the system, Pulse builds the interface, and Titan builds the back end.
Sentinel tests and reviews everything.
Juniors like Nova and Byte take small tasks, and a senior mentor checks their work.
Step one: connect a model.
Open Connections. If you already pay for Claude Code, Codex or Gemini, just sign in to its command-line tool.
Agent HQ uses that subscription directly. No API key needed.
Missing a tool? Click Install, or copy the command.
Ollama and the Magpie gateway are found automatically.

scenes.chapter: Step 2 · A model for every role
lines: Step two: give every role a model.
Under Role defaults, click Fill empty roles.
Each role gets a strong starting model, and you can change any of them.
Step three: open your project.
Click the project switcher, then pick a folder or create a new project.
Agents only read, write and run commands inside that folder.
Now ask for something. In Workspace, switch to Plan, describe the change, and press Send.
Sovereign breaks it into tasks, and gives each one an agent, a complexity, and a model.
Every task shows who chose its model. Here, Sovereign picked Codex, and says why.
Change anything you like. Nothing runs until you click Approve and run.
The team gets to work.
Tasks moves each card across the board.
The graph shows who is working with whom.
And the office shows every agent at their desk, live.
When the work is done, Sentinel reviews it.
Open Changes to see exactly what each agent changed, file by file.
Need a shell? The built-in terminal opens your own shell, right in the project.
So who picks the model for each task? The first rule that applies wins.
One: you, if you chose a model in the plan.
Two: an agent you locked to its own model.
Three: a level you locked in Settings.
Four: Sovereign, which may choose a better model, and tells you why.
Five: your preferred model for that level.
Six: Magpie, which picks the subscription with the most room left.
And seven: Auto, where the best-ranked models take turns.
It's decided fresh for every task. It's not a one-time setup.
You control all of this in Settings, under Models and routing.
Pin a model for simple, standard, or complex work.
Preferred is a starting point Sovereign may change. Locked always wins.
Force my setup locks every pin at once.
To keep one agent on one model, open it, and choose Always this model.
Have more than one subscription? Turn on Let Magpie pick the account.
Agent HQ sets up routing groups in Magpie, and Magpie spreads the work by the quota each account has left.
An account that's almost empty is skipped.
Recent model decisions shows who chose every model.
And the ranking learns from real results, like QA approvals and rejections.
Your team grows with you.
Onboard a junior, and Agent HQ suggests the right mentor.
After every run, agents write lessons from QA and mentor feedback, and you can teach them too.
Decide how much freedom agents have: ask every time, auto-apply approved changes, or full access.
And Reports shows runs, tokens, and estimated cost.
That's Agent HQ.
Install the deb or rpm package from GitHub Releases, connect one subscription, and give your team its first task.
New versions show up right in the app. Just look for the arrow.
